learning_outcomes.text: The student knows and names the different UX characteristics in an existing application. He/she detects UX problems and makes suggestions for improving the UX. He/she names the design trends and styles used.
The student knows the different user testing methods.
The student knows the project flow for developing applications.
The student knows and understands the structure of simple React applications and can improve/supplement/explain the associated code.
The student develops a working application using React and a JSON database.
The student works according to the provided project flow and adjusts his/her actions based on feedback from the client and/or fellow students.
The student designs a proposed solution based on an analysis of existing applications within the framework of the provided design principles. He/she checks the solution against the requirements.
The student uses sketches, wireframes, and prototypes as a means of communication.

The student tests the application during the development process with a view to delivering a successful working whole. He/she tests the functionality and user experience of the application throughout the entire development process.
The student creates a realistic and effective plan for his/her own activities and processes. He/she delivers the project by the proposed deadline.

syllabus_topics: Recent trends and buzzwords in user experience and usability
Implementing a good user interface using a web application
React as a frontend design framework
Supportive exercises for familiarization with technologies
Self-developed, interactive web application using React and Bootstrap/other CSS framework
Project flow from design phase (user stories, sketches, wireframes, prototypes) to development phase (working web application)
assessment_rules: The course is evaluated based on two activities: a theory exam and a lab exam. The theory exam evaluates learning outcomes (1)-(4) and is a written, closed-book test. The lab exam evaluates learning outcomes (5)-(10) and consists of a portfolio and a demonstration of an interactive web application. If a student scores less than 7 on either the theory or lab exam, the maximum overall score for the course is 9/20. For resits, successful partial results for 'GUI Development: Theory' and 'GUI Development: Lab' can be carried over, and students must contact the lecturer to understand the shortcomings of their initial submission.
